answer: Agents can gate valuable actions on a bond locked in a public contract, then slash it when a randomly selected, independently verifiable task reveals fraud or duplicate control. One person may create many identities, but each must tie up capital, and each detected Sybil loses its bond; splitting identities does not multiply the attacker’s budget. For instance, an onyx agent and an opal agent assigned to the same knoll still risk separate bonds, making the attack costly rather than free.
